hypothesis: The queued post-work screen reduced road rounds by 12.1% and edge attempts by 1.5% but added one entry per PE per round and did not improve time. Fusing the bounded heap turn and contribution into the existing one-entry dispatch should retain the fresher snapshot without that callback overhead.
scope: Exploratory follow-up on designated tuning sources only. One exclusive Delta CPU node, 16 processes x 7 workers, 112 workers total, +old-scheduler. Compare a separately built fused binary with two copies of the immediate baseline. Do not reinterpret the rejected held-out post-work screen or promote from these tuning data.

acceptance.road_time: At least 5% geometric-mean improvement and faster than both immediate copies on both road tuning sources.
acceptance.mesh_regression: Worst mesh tuning-source slowdown no larger than the greater of 5% and the duplicate-immediate timing floor.
acceptance.decision: A pass authorizes only a fresh independent confirmation. A failure rejects contribution placement; do not tune further on these sources.

prediction: Fusion retains roughly the 12% round reduction of queued post-work contribution and converts it into at least a 5% road time improvement.
